audit.whatIsWrong: diff said HARD but the tone was the even-matchup yellow and report[14] read 'Even matchup — difficulty 6/10'.
audit.why: 46.37% over 3690 games with the mirror at 57.17% is a hard lane, and the mirror already moved its side to match.
audit.corrected: diffRating 7/10, tone set to the hard-matchup red, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Tryndamere first item and two items against a 46.37% win rate, and called level 1 and level 2 even while whys[0] said the stage tilts to Malphite.
audit.why: The mirror settled it: Tryndamere owns levels 1-3, and from 4-5 onward every stage is Malphite's. The turn is armour — Ground Slam scales its damage off his Armor and cuts your attack speed, so each item he buys improves his offence and your defence problem at once.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite in matched pairs, ratings rescaled, and all seven whys aligned.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appeared anywhere, and the ultimate comparison that decides level 6 was missing entirely.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80 against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100 — yours is back first at every rank, which is the concrete reason to answer his engage rather than dodge it. Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of his max health and recharges only if he goes a few seconds without being hit, so continuous pressure denies it. Ground Slam is a flat 7s. Thunderclap is an auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, spikes[1], spikes[2], early and five phase whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The build advice was 'a little armor pen' with no reason attached.
audit.why: His armour is not only defence — Ground Slam's damage scales off it and its attack-speed cut is what actually blunts a crit build. That is the argument for penetration and against a long extended trade.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] and phases[5].why now say so.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Malphite contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave. Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health but only recharges once you stop hitting him — so do not stop.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Malphite's Unstoppable Force is down.
edits.after: Ground Slam is a flat 7s that cuts your attack speed and scales its damage off his own Armor. Trade between the casts.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Malphite must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Level 3 is your window: his base damage is low, Thunderclap is 10s at rank 1, and your fury crits land before his armour does.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Unstoppable Force's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane closes here: every armour item he buys makes Ground Slam hit harder while blunting your crits. Take the trades now or not at all.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Malphite's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 against his 130s Unstoppable Force — yours comes back first at every rank, so trade ultimates and win the timer.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Unstoppable Force's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker helps you stick, but Ground Slam's attack-speed cut is what really blunts your damage.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Malphite carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in, his armour scales Ground Slam while your crits shrink. Malphite carry threat 7/10 — take objectives, not duels.

edits.before: Level 1 is even but tilts to Malphite — his passive shield blunts your early trades.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — keep hitting him and Granite Shield never gets to recharge.

edits.before: Level 2 stays a skill window as neither champion threatens a kill yet.
edits.after: Level 2 stays yours — his base damage is low and your fury is not.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay yours — this is the pre-armor window where you can shove and punish him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 go to him: his first armour item makes Ground Slam hit harder both ways.

edits.before: Level 6 is even because his R Unstoppable Force knock-up neutralises your all-in threat.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: Unstoppable Force is a point-and-click knock-up you cannot dodge.

edits.before: At first item his armor and Thornmail start turning your crits against you — even at best.
edits.after: At first item his armour and a Thornmail start turning your own crits against you.

edits.before: Late his stacked armor and teamfight engage outscale your crit duel, keeping it a skill floor.
edits.after: Late his stacked armour and teamfight engage outscale you, and the duel stops being close.

edits.before: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — Saved for fights. Lane is fine without it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Unstoppable Force: 130s at rank 1 against your 120s — your ultimate is back first at every rank. - Ground Slam: a flat 7s that cuts your attack speed and scales off his Armor. - Granite Shield: recharges only if you stop hitting him.

edits.before: Track Malphite's Unstoppable Force: Saved for fights. Lane is fine without it. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s to his 130s — yours returns first, so answer his engage and take the next one free.

edits.before: Saved for fights. Lane is fine without it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 130s at rank 1 — your own ultimate is shorter, so trade them and win the timer.

edits.before: That is Malphite's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Thunderclap is an auto reset — the wind-up is the cue to step out, not the cast.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Granite Shield recharges only if you leave him alone for a few seconds.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Unstoppable Force and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how much you take out of levels 1-3 before his armour arrives.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Malphite carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 7/10, Malphite carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: His R Unstoppable Force is a point-and-click knock-up you can't dodge in lane; play at max range, never hug the wall, and hold your E to disengage after he ults.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a point-and-click knock-up you cannot dodge in lane, but it is 130s at rank 1 against your 120s — answer it with Undying Rage and yours is back first.

edits.before: Malphite's armor stacking plus Thornmail turn your crits against you — Bramble/Frozen Heart gut your DPS and your Q sustain can't out-race his passive shield poke.
edits.after: His armour cuts both ways: Thornmail and Frozen Heart gut your crit DPS, while Ground Slam scales its own damage off that Armor and cuts your attack speed every 7s.

edits.before: Early levels are a skill matchup that quietly favours the tank — Malphite's passive shield lets him poke or absorb your trades, and you can't kill through his armor start. Farm cleanly and look only for chip trades where his shield is down.
edits.after: Early levels are yours if you stay on him — Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health but only recharges once you stop hitting him, so keep the pressure constant rather than trading in bursts and letting the rock come back.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are your best and only real window: before his armor and Sunfire come online his base damage is low, so E in, burn Q Bloodlust resets, and shove him under tower. Once he hits 6, his R Unstoppable Force is an undodgeable knock-up — respect it and never hug walls.
edits.after: Level 3 is your best and only real window: before his first armour item his base damage is low, so spin in, burn Bloodlust resets, and shove him under tower. From 4-5 the armour arrives, Ground Slam starts scaling off it, and at 6 his knock-up is point-and-click — respect it and never hug walls.

notes: The kit file tags Seismic Shard and Ground Slam with a grounding flag, but Riot's text for both describes only damage, a move-speed steal and an attack-speed cut. Grounding would matter enormously here — it would turn off Spinning Slash — so I did not assert it anywhere and it should be verified before anyone writes it onto the page. Mocking Shout's attack-damage reduction is close to worthless in this lane since Ground Slam's damage comes off his Armor, and its slow only applies to a back that is turned.
